# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 30 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_030_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 30

**1** Jesus said: "Where there are three gods [ноуте], they are gods.

**2** Where there are two or one, I am with him."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *ноуте*: god, deity; Coptic loan from Greek θεός
- This saying is notoriously difficult and is complicated by P.Oxy 1 lines 11-21 which combines Saying 30 with Saying 77b
- P.Oxy 1 reads: "Where there are three, they are without God. And where there is only one, I say I am with him. Lift the stone and you will find me there; split the wood and I am there."
- The Coptic and Greek versions are significantly different
- The Coptic Saying 30 says "where there are three gods, they ARE gods" (seemingly affirming polytheistic gatherings)
- Many scholars believe the Coptic has a textual corruption; the P.Oxy version ("without God" not "are gods") is preferred by many
- The saying about wood and stone in P.Oxy appears as Saying 77 in the Coptic (split separately)

---
